title: Is £1 less than 50p?
_map: Price it yourself (Y2). Big idea: adding and comparing money. Creative: set prices for his own produce; can a customer buy 3 things with £1?
_story: Ismaeel becomes the shopkeeper and sets prices. A customer has £1 (100p) and wants three things. Can they afford it? Steve thinks £1 is less than 50p because 1 is smaller than 50.
_stepChain: pence (market-stall) → a pound is 100 pence → Steve's 1 < 50 mistake → set prices → add three prices → compare with £1

talk.ask: How did you check if the customer could buy 3 things with £1?
talk.goodAnswer: added the three prices and checked the total was 100p or less.

handsOn: Make price tags for 5 toys. Give a grown-up £1 in coins. Which 3 toys can they buy? Is there any change?

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Ismaeel, today you're the shopkeeper! Ding ding! A customer has come in, with a big gold coin!
This gold coin is one pound. One pound is worth 100 pence! That's the same as ten 10p coins!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Hmm. 1 is smaller than 50. So a one-pound coin must be worth less than 50p!

question.prompt: Is one pound worth less than 50p?
question.onRight: Yes, you caught him! One pound is 100 pence. That's more than 50p!

0.mistake: compared the numbers without the units
0.hint: One pound is how many pence?
0.say: That 1 means one pound, not one penny! One pound is 100 pence, and 100 is more than 50.

narration.text: Here are your prices, shopkeeper! Eggs, 30p. Carrots, 20p. An apple, 10p. A pumpkin, 60p.
The customer wants eggs, carrots, and a pumpkin.

question.prompt: Can they buy all three with one pound?
question.onRight: Yes, you worked it out! 30 and 20 and 60 is 110p. More than 100p!

0.mistake: didn't add all three prices before comparing
0.hint: Add all three: 30, then 20 more, then 60 more. Is it more than 100?
0.say: 30 and 20 make 50. Then 60 more makes 110 pence. That's more than one pound! So they can't buy all three.

question.reveal: 110p is too much! Swap the pumpkin for an apple: 30, 20 and 10 make 60p, with 40p change.

rule.ask: How do you check if someone has enough money? Say it out loud! Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: One pound is 100 pence. Add up the prices, then compare the total with the money you have.

bonus.prompt: Bonus! With one pound, how many 10p apples could you buy?
bonus.reveal: 10 apples! 10 lots of 10p is 100p, one pound.
